text:
St. Louis has handed Philip Broberg the keys. He is playing 24:52 a night, up from 23:21 last season, and topped 28 minutes in three of his last five games, including 29:48 against Utah on Thursday. He is also on the ice for 55% of the Blues' power-play chances, double last season's share, and the results show: 13 points in 19 games, 6 of them on the power play, and his own chances are up sharply.

The Hockey News framed him alongside Luke Hughes as proof of "the reward of paying defensemen with upside." Our numbers agree on the offense and hesitate on the rest. His points per 60 sit above our range for him, the Blues have finished about eight goals better than their chances with him on the ice, and at five on five they are getting only 44% of expected goals with him out there, 8 points worse than without him.

Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among defensemen in value last season, so the talent is not in question. Watch the five-on-five share as those minutes pile up; that is where a breakout either holds or gets exposed.
